title: perf-canary: add Grafana dashboard (p95 latency + tokens/sec) with deploy annotations + drilldowns
author: Felix Schneider
body:
Summary: Adds the v1 Grafana dashboard for the production perf-regression canary. The dashboard is intended for internal triage and alert follow-up: per-model p95 latency + tokens/sec panels, slice filters (region / gpu_sku / runtime_build / scheduler_mode), and deploy annotations so we can correlate regressions with runtime rollouts.

Context: This is part of the perf-canary rollout workstream (ENG-2847). We already have canary traffic tagged with source=perf-canary and runtime_build propagated through the telemetry pipeline; this PR wires up the visual layer in observability-pack so SRE + Runtime have a shared landing page.

Dashboard contents (high level): 1) Overview row: global health indicators and last deploy marker. 2) Per-model p95 latency (ms) time-series with optional baseline overlay (rolling median from detector output when present) and a small "N samples" panel to help spot low-signal periods. 3) Per-model tokens/sec time-series (decode throughput) with streaming vs non-streaming split. 4) Slice explorer row: same metrics but broken out by gpu_sku and scheduler_mode to quickly attribute regressions to fleet heterogeneity vs runtime changes. 5) Drilldowns: panel links jump to (a) a slice-specific view (auto-applies model + region + gpu_sku variables) and (b) the corresponding alert rule in Grafana alerting / runbook link.

Annotations: Adds a dashboard-level annotation query using the runtime deploy event metric (emits runtime_version + git_sha). This is used to render vertical markers labeled like "runtime 1.12.0-rc3 (a1b2c3d)".

Variables / cardinality controls: Variables are limited to model, region, gpu_sku, runtime_build, scheduler_mode. Intentionally *not* exposing kernel_id as a template variable to avoid accidentally encouraging high-cardinality exploration directly from the dashboard; kernel-level details remain in logs/traces and the canary debug export. (See review notes from Thomas Baird below.)

Files changed: - dashboards/perf-canary/perf_canary_overview.json: new dashboard JSON (Grafana). - dashboards/perf-canary/README.md: how to import, required datasources, and variable semantics. - dashboards/_index.json: register the new dashboard for packaging.

Screenshots: Not attached (JSON-only change). You can preview via the staging Grafana folder "Perf Canary" (link in README).

Validation: - Imported into staging Grafana (us-east) against canary metrics namespace; variable dropdowns load in <2s. - Verified annotations render for the last 5 runtime deploys. - Spot checked p95 panel query matches metric spec: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by(le, model, region, gpu_sku, runtime_build, scheduler_mode) (rate(redwood_inference_request_latency_ms_bucket{source="perf-canary"}[5m]))). - Tokens/sec uses the canary-normalized metric (post PR-39157 bugfix in runtime): sum(rate(redwood_inference_tokens_total{source="perf-canary"}[5m])) / sum(rate(redwood_inference_request_duration_seconds_sum{source="perf-canary"}[5m])) (with streaming_mode split).

Follow-ups (not in this PR): - Add a small table panel listing the current detector status per slice ("regressing" / "ok" / "insufficient samples") once ENG-2846 metric output is fully standardized. - Add a "Recent alerts" panel once the alert pipeline exports a stable event metric (SRE asked for this during rollout).

Review conversation (highlights): - Allison Grant: Requested we align panel naming and units with observability standards ("p95 latency (ms)" not "P95"), and add a note about required labels; addressed in README + panel titles. - Logan Wright: Flagged that annotation query should be capped to prevent expensive lookbacks; set max lookback to 14d and used a low-resolution query (1m step) with datasource-side caching. - Nadia Rahman: Asked to ensure p95 computed from buckets not summaries; confirmed and added comment in dashboard JSON "do not switch to summary". Also requested we include a "samples" panel to help interpret noise; added. - Sean Gallagher: Wanted the dashboard to include direct links to runbook and PagerDuty service; added panel links to the runbook URL and alert rule UID, plus a text panel with "what to do first" pointers. - Thomas Baird: Pushed back on adding kernel_id variable; agreed to keep it out to stay within cardinality budget and avoid training folks to do high-cardinality slice browsing in Grafana.

CI: - dashboard-lint: pass - json-schema-check: pass - packager: pass

Merge notes: Squashed as "perf-canary dashboard v1". This should be safe to roll out to prod Grafana immediately; it does not change collectors or alerting rules.
